T-1934: 1729 Prairie's stack behind the rear face, off Taylor 16554 (#1668)

* T-1934: 1729 Prairie's stack behind the rear face, off Taylor 16554

Taylor's no. 16554 shows a stone stack rising behind the house's rear (east)
face between its two rear dormers, which the build did not stand: the last
open item in the conservatory's 16554 record. Built as chimneys.stacks[3]
(u 1.4, v 10.0, top 18.4 m), placed against the dormers because that camera
is not fitted on the house's rear (L-pullman-1729-rear-stack-1934); the house
rebaked and all eleven estate and house match records re-rendered, verdicts
re-judged (the conservatory's 16554 view now matches).

The remaining open item, 16555's house corner about 1 m east of the print's,
is diagnosed in its record: the camera fitted the wing's west end (the house's
east wall) at u -12.12 while the scene places the house's east wall at -11.21;
the 1894 plate reads the same 1 m. That is the house's placement (T-1881) and
stays open, so the ticket's image gate stays open.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* T-1934: re-derive source-use coverage and the 1904 built-so-far walk

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

* T-1934: rebake 1729 Prairie's stack onto dev's house; re-render and re-judge the estate's eleven views; restamp 2009 Prairie's inputs

Dev's #1658 changed the shared K01 frontage generator and rebaked only 1729
Prairie, which left 2009 Prairie's (Mayer) committed mesh stale by input hash
(validate.py --stale red on dev). Rebaked with --only: its mesh bytes are
unchanged; the manifest's input hash is current again.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
